discussion_comments.comment_body: The issue is correct but this is not an acceptable implementation. The idea/guideline is to not to bloat context at any cost. Can you refer how we do it in integrations.go and probably think of a better implementation here?

Thanks for the pointer. I updated the implementation to follow the existing streaming pattern used by the handlers: integration streaming now pre-allocates `BifrostContextKeyTransportPostHookCompleter`, lets `TransportInterceptorMiddleware` publish the post-hook completer into that slot, and passes the logs returned by that completer into the trace completer after the stream drains. This removes the `transportPluginLogsFromFastHTTP` helper and no longer reads transport plugin logs back from `fasthttp` context.

I also applied the same path to passthrough streaming, which was still calling `traceCompleter(nil)`, and updated the regression test to exercise the completer-slot flow instead of seeding logs directly on the context.

Tested with:

```sh
GOWORK=/private/tmp/bifrost-streamlogs-work/go.work go test ./bifrost-http/integrations -run 'TestHandleStreamingRetainsTransportPluginLogs' -count=1
```

Fixed — removed the process-global `FallbackWarningHook`/`Init()`-wiring entirely and threaded each provider's own instance-bound `logger` field directly into `ToChatRequest` instead, so warnings are always attributed to the correct Bifrost instance. To preserve the exported zero-argument call shape for existing Go SDK consumers (per a follow-up codex review), `logger` is variadic/optional rather than a required new parameter. Verified: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `go test ./schemas/... ./providers/...` all clean across every touched package.

Fixed in 313be8173 — all `logger.Warn`/`Info(fmt.Sprintf(...))` calls in this closure and in `resolveMatViewRefreshInterval` now pass format args directly (`%v` for errors). Kept the dialector check: it predates this PR, is mirrored in the matview boot closure, and removing harmless defensive code is out of scope here.
